optimization_notes: optimized.py: `Graph().parse(...)` is chained; subjects() gets positional arguments; the four dead "NA"/0 initialisations go; `as e` (never read) goes; the last three try blocks, which differ only in the property and the conversion, become one loop over (name, convert) in the same read order. `break` with a for/else replaces their `continue`, so the message (f"Error converting {name}={val} …", same text) and the skip are the same, and `val` is read the same way (from the previous read if graph.value raises). The single-element `for lang in ['lv']` becomes `lang = 'lv'`. The solution-text concatenation becomes a list over the property path `problemSolution / solutionText` joined with '\n\n' (the path walks the same nested objects() in the same order, duplicates kept). The client call is chained, and the return tuple loses its parentheses.
One visible difference: the data_object keys now come in read order (olympiadType before problemGrade). Dict equality, which is what the driver compares through the fake client, does not see it.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph as graph` + `graph.parse(...)` replaces `graph = Graph().parse(...)`; subjects(RDF.type, …) becomes `m{ ?subj a {…Problem} }`; the problemText loop and the path read become `m{ {subj} {P} ?obj }` and `m{ {subj} {A / B} ?text }`, the same length as objects() once @graph is in scope.
Rule 4: the four graph.value(subj, P) reads stay Python (`m{ … }.first()` is 4 tokens longer each).
No exception to the symmetry: the try loop, the path and the join of solution texts are all in optimized.py.
the `@prefix rdf:` line in optimized.ldpy is translated.ldpy's header, kept byte for byte; `a` makes it unused in the region, which is why it is declared but the header variant drops it.
header_optimization_notes: Python: URIRef and Namespace go (`from rdflib import Graph, RDF`).
LD Python: the whole rdflib import goes (no Graph or RDF left outside the islands: `@graph as graph`, `a`), and so does the `@prefix rdf:` line, which `a` makes unused; only `import sys` stays.
